newsitem.title: USA: SNET restructuring may affect '98 earnings.
newsitem.headline: SNET restructuring may affect '98 earnings.

text.p: Southern New England Telecommunications Corp (SNET) said Wednesday that Connecticut regulators' rejection of part of the company's proposed restructuring could have a "significant effect" on its 1998 earnings.

It was responding to the Department of Public Utility Control (DPUC)'s rejection of SNET's proposal to transfer all of its retail customers to its affiliate, SNET America Inc (SAI), effective on January 1, 1998.
The DPUC said it will instead send ballots to SNET retail customers next year to select a local exchange carrier.

"Our retail subsidiary, newly certified as a local exchange carrier, will have the pricing and marketing flexibility to compete on an equal footing with other CLECs (Certified Local Exchange Carriers) in Connecticut," Miglio said.
The DPUC said SNET will become a wholesale-only company a year from now, selling services and facilities to competitive providers, but not to end-users.
Retail service to end-use customers will be provided by competitive local exchange telephone companies, including a SNET affiliate, the Department said.

The DPUC said it rejected SNET's proposal to automatically transfer all of its retail customers directly to SAI because "since SNET has chosen to cease serving retail customers, fairness requires that no one company, especially a SNET affiliate, automatically have an advantage in the number of retail customers."
SNET currently serves more than two million lines and 1.4 million customers, nearly all of Connecticut's telephone customers.
